title: Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl, the Emperor's cousin and ruler of the Ṭāʾifa of Shalamanka since 1395, dies at fifty-three

Maxorata on Fuerteventura in the Canaries becomes a settlement of the crown: 7,900 people, most of them Guanche islanders of their own faith. With them the tribes enter the empire as an estate of their own

data.tribes: the tribes estate: under 1% of power on 31 December 1415; to be followed only above 3–4% (Trent)

title: Three months after Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl's death, the Ṭāʾifa of Shalamanka is taken into the crown: its 21 towns and 347,000 people, from Shalamanka, Ávila and Ciudad Rodrigo to Plasencia and Coria, become lands of the crown

data.note: not planned: the annexation went through on the ruler's death. Trent accepts it as fitting the pattern: the far north handed to ṭāʾifas, the lands south of it integrated into the crown

title: The estates at the end of 1415: the crown holds about a quarter of the power of the state, the dhimmī more than a fifth, the burghers and the umarāʾ each nearly a fifth, the ʿulamāʾ a tenth. The umarāʾ are a quarter content and climbing back toward two in five
source: Trent's estates panel, 31 December 1415; save of 1 January 1416
